name: Jewish Autonomism
summary: Jewish Autonomism held that the Jews are a nation in the present, sustained by culture, history and communal institutions rather than a territory or state, and should have legally recognised national-cultural self-government within the multinational states where they live. It rejected both assimilation and political Zionism as the main answer, while demanding full civil and political rights for individual Jews. Its social program was liberal-democratic and largely non-socialist in Dubnow's own version, although the Bund adopted autonomy in a socialist form.
scope: The mainstream Dubnowist strand: Simon Dubnow's Letters on Old and New Judaism (1897-1906) and Nationalism and History, and the Folkspartei (Jewish People's Party) he founded in 1906. The Bund's socialist autonomism, Austro-Marxist personal autonomy and American diaspora nationalism (Kallen, Janowsky) are not the basis. Since the sources cover national, religious and rights questions but rarely economics, most economic and modern-social answers are low-confidence inferences.

sources.title: Simon Dubnow
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Dubnow's agnosticism, equal-rights and voting demands, self-defence against pogroms, and Zionism as a beautiful messianic dream.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Never addressed; a left-liberal Folkspartei adherent would likely accept public provision, but sources give no program on health.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the Folkspartei's liberal-democratic reform outlook; no wage policy appears in the sources consulted.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Autonomism was a national-cultural doctrine with no economic theory, so adherents were split or indifferent.

public-ownership.rationale: Dubnow did not believe in socialism as a solution (s4 notes he opposed the Marxist Bund), so broad nationalisation is unlikely to be endorsed.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Fiscal policy was outside the doctrine; the liberal Folkspartei gives no basis for a firm answer.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred: liberal-democratic autonomists accepted workers' organisation, though they put national unity above class organisation.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property was not an autonomist concern; liberal commitments pull one way, communal solidarity the other.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Never addressed; no evident position either way.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from communal self-help traditions and liberal reformism; welfare cuts are not part of the doctrine and sit badly with community-care ideals.

worker-ownership.rationale: Dubnow rejected socialism as the answer to Jewish problems, so collective worker ownership is not a central aim.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the rights-based liberal outlook of a persecuted minority wary of state power.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy lay far outside a 1900s national-cultural doctrine, and nothing in Dubnow's liberalism settles it either way.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Autonomists sought minority protection in law, but speech limits were not discussed; split.

strong-leader.rationale: Dubnow's program assumed democratic, constitutional multinational states and elected communal bodies, not strongman rule.

state-harmful.rationale: Autonomism relied on states recognising minority rights and a constitutional order; it was not anti-statist.

limit-guns.rationale: Dubnow backed Jewish self-defence against pogroms, but gun control as such was never discussed.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred: a minority exposed to state violence in the Russian Empire would distrust expanded coercive powers.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not discussed by autonomists; liberal and communal-moral instincts would split adherents.

decide-locally.rationale: Autonomism devolves cultural power to national communities rather than territorial localities, so it is neutral on local-versus-national government.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from liberal-humanist reformism; not discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: Dubnow was a secular agnostic but valued communal continuity; adherents split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: A question of later decades; the doctrine gives no guidance and adherents would split between liberal and traditional views.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anachronistic; adherents ranged from secular to traditional.

more-religion-public.rationale: Dubnow saw religion as a national defence no longer needed after emancipation, and Jewish identity as historical-cultural rather than religious.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; autonomism's own concern was minority rights, which suggests mild sympathy but no program.

gender-social-construct.rationale: A later academic debate unconnected to autonomism, leaving adherents without a settled view.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Protecting the national individuality and cultural creativity of the Jewish people was the stated aim of autonomism.

gradual-change.rationale: Autonomists sought constitutional change through legal means and the Duma, yet also demanded radical recognition of national rights; split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred: a diaspora minority needing refuge and equal rights would oppose restriction.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Dubnow welcomed the Paris 1919 minority-rights treaties, but supranational power as such was not a theme.

free-trade.rationale: Autonomism had no trade policy, and a landless diaspora people has no clear stake either way.

nation-first.rationale: Autonomists were non-territorial and relied on international minority guarantees, which fits poorly with putting one's own state first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; minority-treaty enforcement hints at some sympathy, but no explicit position.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; migration of Jews was a practical matter, not a principle.

limit-growth.rationale: Ecological limits were not a concern of early twentieth-century Jewish politics, so no view can be inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate change is anachronistic for the doctrine; only a vague liberal-progressive leaning could be guessed.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Dubnow's progress was cultural-historical, not technological, so adherents are not committed either way.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power is anachronistic for the movement and no principle bears on it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Dubnow worked within the Duma and legal organisation and rejected the Bund's class-struggle line, which suggests a reformist stance.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from its democratic communal institutions and elected national assembly.

central-planning.rationale: Dubnow rejected socialism as the solution; planned economy not part of the doctrine.

socialized-markets.rationale: The doctrine had no economic program; Dubnow rejected socialism but the Folkspartei was social-reformist, so adherents split.

land-value-tax.rationale: A specific fiscal reform never taken up by autonomists.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Autonomists left tax questions to ordinary politics, so nothing can be inferred.

basic-income.rationale: A modern welfare idea absent from the movement's literature.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade protection was not addressed and a diaspora minority had no obvious national industry to protect.

state-directs-investment.rationale: No economic-planning view; Dubnow's rejection of socialism points mildly against, but not firmly.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Distribution of property was not an autonomist concern.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Dubnow did not believe in socialism, and abolishing wage labour is a Marxist-communist aim foreign to autonomism.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions were never discussed in the doctrine.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Autonomism organised nations as communities, not employers and workers, and was liberal-democratic; state-recognised class bodies are not part of it.

one-party-rule.rationale: Dubnow founded a party that sought democratic Jewish self-rule within a democratic Russia, and the doctrine assumes pluralist constitutional states.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred: Dubnow demanded equal rights and Duma participation against tsarist autocracy.

democracy-best.rationale: The Folkspartei sought legal recognition of Jewish nationality in a democratic government and Dubnow demanded extended democratic rights.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed; the model was elected communal councils and a national assembly.

workers-councils.rationale: Dubnow rejected the Bund's socialist line, and the model was elected national communal bodies, not class councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Autonomism sought rights inside existing states instead of separation, though it did not rule out others' self-determination.

natural-rulers.rationale: Inferred from a democratic doctrine demanding equal rights for all.

political-violence-never.rationale: Dubnow organised self-defence against pogroms but favoured legal politics; split.

war-builds-character.rationale: A stateless spiritual-nation theory stressing ethical mission over political power is hostile to glorifying war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Dubnow was agnostic and saw religion as no longer needed as a national defence, though autonomy let communities run religious affairs.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Dubnow founded identity on history and culture, not religion, and the program was secular constitutional autonomy.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Unaddressed; autonomism relied on state minority guarantees.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred: non-territorial nation with no army has no basis for the aim.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Autonomists envisaged multinational states where nations coexist; they claimed national rights without a nation-state.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Dubnow saw history as not reducible to economics and criticised the Bund's focus on class struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The program demanded equal rights and national autonomy, not equality of material outcomes, and social-economic views were split.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Unaddressed, though cultural autonomy for minorities suggests partial sympathy.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations for colonialism are outside the doctrine, though group-rights thinking gives mild sympathy.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred: Jews as dispersed in many states; autonomism sought rights within states, not religion-based political unions.

self-interest-moral.rationale: No ethical stance on self-interest; Dubnow stressed an ethical mission of the Jews but not a view on egoism.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Dubnow demanded individual civil rights plus national rights; community duty above rights is not stated.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics did not figure in the doctrine.

limit-population.rationale: Population control was not an issue for the movement, which cared about Jewish survival and numbers.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred from a modernising, education-reforming outlook.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Rapid technological disruption is not an autonomist theme.

human-enhancement.rationale: Transhumanist ideas are anachronistic for early twentieth-century autonomists.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; the doctrine's picture of government is elected councils and national assemblies.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; only a general wariness of state power can be inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Dubnow sought a modernised communal order, not restoration; Orthodox rigidity was among his targets.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Autonomists were committed to a doctrine but also pragmatic coalition builders, so adherents would split.

direct-action.rationale: Autonomists pursued Duma elections and legal party politics.

means-match-ends.rationale: The movement did not discuss prefigurative politics.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A historical theory of progress to spiritual nationhood is incompatible with this.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marxist-utopian aim foreign to a non-socialist doctrine.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not part of a doctrine that rejected socialism.

production-for-use.rationale: Not part of a doctrine that rejected socialism.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Dubnow rejected socialist theory and the Bund's class-first outlook.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Dubnow opposed the Marxist Bund and sought democratic constitutional autonomy.

collective-farming.rationale: Collective agriculture is a socialist aim that Dubnow's non-socialist doctrine did not adopt.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: This is Marxist-Leninist theory; Dubnow rejected socialist explanations of history.

taxation-theft.rationale: Autonomism envisaged communal bodies with taxing authority and constitutionally recognised self-rule.

harm-principle.rationale: Autonomists were liberal-minded but never stated a Millian principle, so the answer is a guess.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Autonomism claims rights for nations as groups, with citizens holding rights both as individuals and as members of their national groups.

conscription.rationale: Jewish conscription in the Russian Empire was a grievance, but autonomism has no general view on military service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Dubnow demanded voting and civil rights where Jews lived rather than emigration.

state-as-business.rationale: Unaddressed; inferred as alien to its rights-based minority politics.

positive-liberty.rationale: The doctrine focuses on group rights and gives no position on material preconditions of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Conspiratorial claims about elite institutions are foreign to a minority-defence doctrine and Dubnow himself was a scholar.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Dubnow defined the Jews as a historical-cultural nation, not a biological race.

organic-representation.rationale: Autonomism's communal bodies resemble representation by community, but it demanded party politics and Duma elections as well.

total-state.rationale: Autonomism was premised on limiting state power through self-governing national communities.

national-rebirth.rationale: Dubnow stressed continuity and survival rather than rebirth, though cultural renewal was part of the program.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal loyalty is foreign to a constitutional program.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom contradicts the equal civil rights Dubnow demanded for all citizens.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology was not addressed, though Dubnow was a historian committed to objective scholarship.

universal-morality.rationale: Dubnow described the Jews as a spiritual nation with an ethical mission, implying universal ethical aims.

single-common-good.rationale: Autonomism accepts coexisting national groups within states rather than a single common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Dubnow called the restoration of a Jewish state a pseudo-messianic adventure and held Zionism could not solve diaspora problems.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Dubnow came to accept Palestine as one cultural centre, but a right of return was not part of autonomism.

revive-national-language.rationale: Autonomists centred Yiddish, the living language, as the language of Jewish culture; Hebrew revival as state language belongs to Zionism.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Industrial democracy was not addressed, and Dubnow's distance from socialism leaves it open.

school-vouchers.rationale: Autonomism wanted Jewish national schools, but funding mechanisms were not specified.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Macroeconomic policy is outside the doctrine.

economic-freedom.rationale: The autonomists linked political freedom to national and civil rights rather than to market freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Dubnow demanded constitutional rights and laws.

national-self-determination.rationale: Autonomists asserted national rights without requiring a state of one's own, and explicitly differed from Zionism on this.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred: reliance on international minority guarantees.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Dubnow was agnostic and historical, but valued Hasidism as creative expression; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from a minority-rights outlook that rejects distinguishing residents by origin.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality was not in the doctrine; communal charity traditions give no clear answer.

class-collaboration.rationale: Dubnow criticised the Bund's class-struggle emphasis at the cost of Jewish national unity.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving the national cultural inheritance was central to autonomism.

dominated-front.rationale: A geopolitical front of dominated states does not fit a non-territorial nation without a state.

workers-nation.rationale: Autonomists put the Jewish nation, not an international or national working class, first.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from the liberal demand for equal rights, though traditional-minded adherents might differ.

ban-interest.rationale: Dubnow's liberal outlook and Jewish economic history make a legal ban on interest unlikely.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Dubnow demanded full and equal rights for Jews and opposed discrimination.

state-class-instrument.rationale: This is the Marxist theory of the state; Dubnow opposed the Marxist Bund and sought legal rights through the state.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is anachronistic for the movement.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Dubnow called assimilation national suicide and defended minority cultural rights, a principle autonomists extend to minorities.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy of this kind is foreign to the doctrine and targets minorities.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred: minority representation interest and democratic liberal commitments.

national-mission.rationale: Dubnow gave the Jews an ethical mission, not a state exporting its government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Feminist social theory is not part of autonomism, though a secular liberal might partly agree.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Autonomism does not make a populist claim about elites, though it opposed tsarist authorities.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from the pogrom experience, which led Dubnow to organise self-defence and demand legal protection.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Autonomism envisaged state backing for national schools and rights.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Dubnow opposed assimilation, but through culture, not discouraging marriage by law or pressure; liberal outlook rejects racial hierarchy.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Dubnow demanded full and equal rights for all Russian Jews.

socialism-one-country.rationale: An internal Marxist debate on which autonomism takes no side.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Autonomists opposed a separate state; no position on settler-colonial theory.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal autonomy gives national communities their own institutions within the state.

restrict-conversion.rationale: A liberal minority doctrine would oppose state limits on religious choice, though Dubnow opposed assimilation culturally.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A Hindu religious demand with no connection to Jewish autonomism, whose own religious law permits slaughter.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Autonomists wanted Jewish national schools, but state school policy was not specified.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is a Soviet theory of the socialist state; autonomism is not a socialist doctrine.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Folkspartei sought recognition within a democratic government by elected assemblies and Dubnow demanded democratic rights.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims are not discussed by autonomists.

population-transfer.rationale: Autonomism is premised on minorities remaining in the states where they live with national rights.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: No stated view on non-aggression, though the program sought rights by legal, non-violent means.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Dubnow's account was a cultural-historical development of nations to spiritual form.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Autonomists wanted open democratic politics but did not discuss banning parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican theory not found in autonomist writings, though the concern with arbitrary power over minorities resembles it.

vanguard-party.rationale: Dubnow opposed Marxist parties such as the Bund and founded a mass democratic party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Class was secondary for Dubnow, who criticised the Bund's focus on it, but the doctrine did not oppose helping the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy remote from the movement.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour law was not addressed; Dubnow's criticism of class-struggle focus is not a call for restriction.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed; Dubnow located Jewish hardship in discrimination, not demography.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Autonomism assumes multinational states in which nationalities coexist with autonomy.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred: elections and democratic communal bodies.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Minority protections were central; suspension is incompatible.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Economic controls were not part of the doctrine.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred from a doctrine demanding democratic freedoms.

party-commands-army.rationale: The doctrine assumes democratic constitutional states in which armed forces are not party instruments.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from the autonomist demand that minorities enjoy full citizenship where they live.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: A socialist-populist measure not addressed by the autonomists.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party organisation was not a doctrinal matter for autonomists.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Unaddressed, though it favours multinational frameworks.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Christian church governance is outside Jewish autonomism.

clerical-rule.rationale: Dubnow held Jewish identity rested on culture, not religious authority.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from the movement's commitment to free cultural creativity, especially in Yiddish and Hebrew.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from constitutional democratic commitments, though the doctrine does not discuss it.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall mechanisms are not part of the autonomist program.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: A stateless nation takes no position on military alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Abolishing rental is a radical socialist idea that Dubnow's liberal doctrine would reject.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred: Jewish diaspora life centred in towns and cities.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Autonomism does not seek territorial reunification and accepts nations living within existing states.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Dubnow was a scholar and championed modernised education.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Autonomism assumes equal national rights for all nationalities in a multinational state.

death-penalty.rationale: Criminal punishment was not addressed by the movement.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Autonomists wanted national schools, but sex education is anachronistic and not discussed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Dubnow was a secular historian who modernised Jewish education, which makes creationism in schools unlikely.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; traditional and secular adherents would split.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Dubnow demanded citizenship rights for Jews where they lived.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language and education rights, especially for Yiddish, were central to the autonomist demands.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Autonomy gives communities their own religious affairs, but individual exemptions from general law were not discussed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's argument is not found in autonomist sources.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from democratic and Duma-oriented politics.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Democratic rights were central to Dubnow's program.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: International aid was not part of the movement's concerns.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic and irrelevant to a stateless people.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Constitutional design beyond minority rights was not set out.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions were outside the doctrine.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Autonomists held no territorial claims, but the question was not addressed.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: No stated property theory; a communal ethic and liberal rights pull in different directions.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Dubnow died in 1941 and the question was outside his doctrine.

precautionary-principle.rationale: An environmental-policy principle that postdates the movement.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance obligations are not an autonomist concern.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Territorial disputes between states were outside the doctrine.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Communities managed their own religious affairs under autonomy.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Head-of-state design is outside the program.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from minority-rights outlook that opposes coercing a group against its will.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy for a group inside a larger state is the autonomist model, though here territorial.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Dubnow demanded equal rights against tsarist autocracy.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not part of the doctrine.

character-from-environment.rationale: Dubnow stressed history and culture shaping a people, but the question concerns individuals and is not addressed.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Autonomism requires constitutional recognition of minority rights, binding rulers.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic and unconnected to the doctrine.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-government theory is not part of autonomism.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from the democratic and scholarly character of the movement, which had no cult of leaders.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court policy is anachronistic for the movement.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: An internal Marxist-Leninist debate, and Dubnow rejected class struggle as the main frame.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform was not an autonomist demand, though Jewish land restrictions in Russia were a grievance.

refugee-return.rationale: Return of refugees was not addressed by the doctrine.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Autonomists claimed no territory and defined nations as non-territorial.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Dubnow was agnostic and treated religion as a matter for communities, not state coercion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitments of secular autonomists, who did not support compelling dress.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not part of the doctrine.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Autonomism is non-territorial and works within states.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Autonomism is precisely personal national-cultural autonomy for dispersed communities within states, without a state of their own.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Dubnow and the autonomists saw the diaspora as the Jewish home and demanded civil rights in the countries of residence.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Dubnow thought history could not be reduced to economics and described a three-stage cultural development of nations.

no-bailouts.rationale: Public finance questions were not addressed.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Autonomism seeks constitutionally recognised minority rights that majorities cannot override.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are a later idea and the doctrine is silent.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarky is foreign to a dispersed people whose survival relied on contact across many states.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: International trade rules were not addressed.

moral-incentives.rationale: A Maoist and Guevarist notion foreign to a liberal national-cultural doctrine.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Dubnow worked through Duma participation and legal organisation rather than insurrection.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from the demand for full equal rights for all, which opposes inherited legal privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Dubnow stressed national history as the basis of Jewish identity and demanded national schools.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from principle of equal national rights.

patriotic-education.rationale: Autonomists wanted national schools to teach Jewish culture, but loyalty to a state flag is not theirs.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is a late, American question the doctrine does not address.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not part of autonomism.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: A Marxist crisis-theory debate that autonomism does not engage.

former-empire-influence.rationale: A great-power question irrelevant to a stateless people.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory remedy foreign to a diaspora doctrine that relies on exchange across borders.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist concept outside autonomist thought.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: A persecuted minority demanding equal rights opposes it.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Autonomism seeks constitutional entrenchment of minority rights, and Dubnow welcomed the post-1919 treaty guarantees.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial borders were not addressed by Jewish autonomism.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from democratic program and Duma participation.

minority-veto.rationale: Autonomism seeks minority protection, not individual vetoes.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Dubnow supported Duma participation and a democratic legislature.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics not addressed by the movement.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; Jewish law on humane slaughter exists but autonomists were largely secular.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Aristocratic duty is not addressed, though communal charity was a feature of kehillot.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Dubnow founded a party and joined the 1905 political organisations.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory belongs to later Marxist thought that autonomism did not share.

native-born-offices.rationale: Dubnow demanded equal rights for all citizens, including Jews as minority.

party-own-road.rationale: An internal Communist debate on which autonomism takes no side.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development economics is outside the movement.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Autonomism makes no territorial claims for nations, so irredentism has no place in it.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the equal-rights, multinational framework, which resists ranking groups by descent.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Dubnow died in 1941 and the question lay beyond his doctrine, though it fits sympathies.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Dubnow died in 1941, before this comparison became a political question.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American historiography is outside the movement.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed, though Dubnow's historical consciousness suggests respect for heritage.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: A modern gender-policy debate that the movement never touched.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: A modern gender-policy debate that the movement never touched.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Dubnow was a European liberal who held that Jewish autonomy would suit modern multinational states, but the claim is about civilisations in general.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's reliance on civilian constitutional government and minority guarantees.

paid-care-work.rationale: A later feminist demand not discussed in the movement.

filial-duty.rationale: Family ethics were not addressed in the sources, though Jewish tradition values it.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service recruitment was not addressed, apart from demands that Jews be admitted to state posts.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Family law was left to communities under autonomy; no view on divorce grounds.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Not part of the program, which relied on ordinary elected communal councils.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Communal land tenure belongs to agrarian socialist movements, not to Dubnow's liberal doctrine.

single-official-language.rationale: Language rights for minorities, Yiddish above all, were central autonomist demands.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from minority outlook, where Jews were restricted from owning land.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anti-discrimination law of the late twentieth century is outside the movement.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumer culture was not a concern of the doctrine.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred: a stateless people seeking legal rights has no such policy, and Dubnow favoured legal means.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from principle of minority national rights.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying and campaign finance were outside the movement's concerns.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: diaspora institutions relied on international support.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Autonomists wanted a numerically viable national community, but state incentives were not discussed.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from a minority-rights outlook that opposes local limits on who may own land, a past Jewish grievance.

job-guarantee.rationale: A modern economic proposal outside the doctrine.

democratic-peace.rationale: International-relations theory not discussed, though autonomists hoped democracy and minority treaties would secure peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred from a constitutional program based on legal rights and obligations.

non-intervention.rationale: Autonomists welcomed international minority-rights treaties, which involve external oversight.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure was a Bund and socialist concern, not an autonomist one.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Autonomism is the defence of minorities against such charges, and Dubnow organised against pogroms.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: autonomy let communities regulate marriage under law, so legal abolition is unlikely.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the democratic and constitutional commitments of the Folkspartei.

informal-organisation.rationale: Dubnow built formal parties and national communal institutions.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Welcomed international minority treaties over state sovereignty.

religious-nation.rationale: Dubnow defined Jewry as a historical-cultural nation, not a religious one.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tributary diplomacy has no place in a democratic minority-rights doctrine.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Territorial fiscal federalism is not part of non-territorial autonomism.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: A Marxist formulation that the movement did not address.

defeat-communism.rationale: Dubnow opposed Marxist parties but the doctrine did not discuss communism as a global opponent.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public service delivery models were not addressed.

religion-illusion.rationale: Dubnow was agnostic but regarded religion as an expression of national reality and valued Hasidism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Dubnow rejected socialism and held that history was not economically determined, but no appraisal of capitalism is stated.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed; Dubnow's non-socialist view suggests doubt but nothing explicit.

socialized-care.rationale: Socialising housework belongs to socialist feminism and does not fit a non-socialist doctrine.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: autonomists fostered Yiddish as a hybrid living language.

treaties-binding.rationale: Dubnow welcomed treaty-based minority protections as binding guarantees.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Unaddressed, though communal self-government is partly analogous.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: opposed to majority dominance over minorities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: No stated third way economically, though Dubnow rejected socialism and the doctrine is not a market creed.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Dubnow rejected Zionist territorial claim, calling restoration a pseudo-messianic adventure.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Dubnow himself was murdered in the Holocaust, and the Holocaust ended autonomism as a popular concept.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from the liberal outlook of secular autonomists, though the question is anachronistic.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Autonomism was a democratic minority doctrine.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Dubnow was agnostic and secular-historical in his view.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from equal national rights principle.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic doctrine with no counterpart in Jewish autonomism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Foreign to a secular-national doctrine that sought rights within existing states.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Communal self-government by elected bodies suggests participatory sympathies.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectionality is a late concept the movement did not address.

assisted-dying.rationale: A bioethical debate far outside early autonomism.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The Folkspartei combined liberal democracy with national claims, but the movement made no statement on the left-right axis.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxian concept not discussed in autonomist writing.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Singling out a faith for exclusion contradicts a doctrine built on minority rights.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Dubnow was agnostic, placed national life on historical and cultural, not divine, grounds, and sought democratic self-government.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed, and autonomists favoured both secular and communal religious freedom.

social-market-economy.rationale: Never addressed, though a liberal reformist adherent might find it congenial.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not addressed; Dubnow supported Jewish self-defence only against pogroms.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: A stateless nation has no foreign-policy position on blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from the democratic and elective program of the Folkspartei.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: A mutualist proposal that autonomism did not address.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: International finance is outside the doctrine.

property-franchise.rationale: Dubnow demanded universal equal rights, including voting rights.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist idea outside the movement.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept not discussed by Dubnow, who rejected Marxism as an explanation of history.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A socialist critique that the movement did not make, though it valued a free Jewish press.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from the constitutional guarantees that autonomism requires.

racial-franchise.rationale: Dubnow demanded equal voting rights for Jews.

online-participation.rationale: Internet deliberation is far outside early twentieth-century autonomism, so no view is inferable.

open-government-data.rationale: Open-data transparency is a modern idea that autonomist sources never raise.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred; assimilation was opposed by culture rather than law.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Autonomism is the defence of a minority against such pressure.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition-based deliberation is a late idea not found in the movement.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Dubnow modernised Jewish education and criticised Orthodox rigidity.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; Dubnow focused on national and civil rights rather than wealth.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Dubnow wanted communities to manage their religious affairs freely.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: An anarchist idea alien to a doctrine that relies on state legal protections for minorities.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Autonomism proposes nationalities with their own autonomy sharing a multinational state.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Communal self-help was an autonomist theme, but the doctrine did not oppose state aid.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is a modern idea absent from the movement.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk is a modern concern absent from the movement, which worried about Jewish survival instead.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; autonomists were mostly secular and left religious matters to communities.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Family law was not addressed by the movement.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the minority-rights outlook that gives residents a voice in local affairs.

rent-control.rationale: Housing policy was outside the doctrine.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; a liberal scholarly outlook favours protecting authors' works.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Militarised youth organisation is foreign to the civic and cultural autonomist program.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear basing is a post-1945 question and Dubnow died in 1941.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign basing is not an issue for a stateless diasporic movement.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed in doctrine, but sympathy likely.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Distributive theory is not part of the doctrine.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Dubnow organised Jewish self-defence against pogroms.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Dubnow described the Jews as a nation continuing through tribal, political and spiritual stages.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Not addressed, though communal memory of persecution was important to Dubnow's historical outlook.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Dubnow's account of nations is historical and secular, not a cosmic struggle of good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Dubnow came to accept Ahad Ha'am's idea of a cultural centre in Palestine as one centre among many.

culture-before-state.rationale: Autonomism builds national cultural institutions without a state at all.

god-not-male.rationale: Religious language was not an autonomist concern.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist theology is later and unrelated to autonomism.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine's defence of minorities against discrimination, including in economic life.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Autonomism is non-territorial, so merging regions for a people is not part of it.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the liberal outlook, which would favour organisations independent of party control.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A socialist criterion that Dubnow, who did not believe in socialism, would not adopt.

municipal-property.rationale: A municipal-socialist or communalist aim not shared by Dubnow's liberal doctrine.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Autonomism has some structural analogy, but not addressed.

family-wage.rationale: Wage policy for families was not discussed in autonomist sources.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Longevity research is a modern topic the movement never addressed.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Digital payments are far outside the movement, so no view can be inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online identity is a modern question outside autonomist thought.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from liberal outlook demanding individual rights.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Dubnow called the Jews a spiritual nation with an ethical mission, which suggests a spiritual dimension, but the claim is about humans generally.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetic engineering of crops postdates the movement and no principle bears on it.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning and ecology were not autonomist topics, though Jewish life was largely urban.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Dubnow held Jews as a national, not racial, group.

racial-pride.rationale: Dubnow defined Jews as a cultural nation and promoted national dignity, but not racial pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: A stateless nation has no stated war policy.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Language was central to autonomist nationhood, though Dubnow also said Jews had lost a unifying language.

communal-electorates.rationale: Personal autonomy had Jewish citizens with their own national assembly.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Conspiracy claims about foreign powers have no place in a minority-rights doctrine.

free-public-college.rationale: Higher-education finance was not addressed, though autonomists campaigned for Jewish access to schooling.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxation is a late-century idea outside the doctrine.

future-generations.rationale: Environmental duty is anachronistic, though Dubnow stressed continuity across generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Difference feminism is not addressed in the sources on autonomism.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed, though Dubnow welcomed the public minority treaties.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Dubnow supported Jewish self-defence organisations against pogroms but state policy was not discussed.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Refusal of war orders was not an autonomist position, which worked through legal politics.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed by the movement, which prioritised national over class organisation.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal constitutionalism is not part of the doctrine.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Global economic restructuring was not a theme for a movement focused on minority rights within states.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Not addressed, though autonomy of communities might suggest sympathy.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Autonomism is a non-territorial doctrine seeking rights within existing states, so it has no basis for territorial expansion.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Anachronistic and never addressed by Dubnow or the Folkspartei; nothing in the sources bears on valuing nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: Dubnow saw the Jewish nation as an enduring historical-spiritual community that gives life meaning, but he was agnostic and secular, so 'sacred' fits only loosely.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic; the sources do not touch on education finance.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: the movement sought minority self-government within multinational states and framed grievances as denial of civil and national rights, not regional exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from Dubnow's liberal demand for equal rights for all individuals; sources do not discuss human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stressed community-run schools and press in Yiddish, not state-funded media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Dubnow treated Judaism as a historical-national culture, not a universal spiritual claim; no position on religious universalism is inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: Dubnow's liberal non-socialist program is inferred to oppose guaranteed prices; an urban diaspora people had little farm interest.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic for a movement that peaked before 1939; nothing can be inferred.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Bund adopted autonomism with a socialist workers' party while Dubnow's Folkspartei was liberal; adherents split.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the movement's liberal-democratic rights stance; anachronistic.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the demand for full civil and political equality in the Folkspartei's liberal-democratic program.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Autonomists backed Yiddish and Hebrew as national languages alongside state languages; the statement is not addressed.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; no inference is possible.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The program demanded elected communal self-government, so an official chiefly role is inferred to be rejected.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The program's priority was civil and national liberties, from which environmental priority over liberty is inferred to be rejected.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: A liberal rights-based program is inferred to favour judicial discretion; not documented.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Autonomists wanted Jews to keep their own languages while using state languages; inferred as split.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Dubnow's liberal Folkspartei did not address union membership and the Bund's socialist version differs, so adherents are split.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed; Dubnow's concern for protecting minority voters from exclusion suggests wariness of restrictions, inferred at low confidence.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Autonomism demanded equal rights for all Jewish groups as a national minority and a secular-style legal order, so no one confession should rule, though Dubnow's sources do not state it directly.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Dubnow demanded equal rights and voting for Jews under constitutional government, which points to elections as the test of democracy, though he also wanted minority rights alongside.

premarital-sex.rationale: Dubnow was agnostic and secular-minded, but the sources never discuss sexual morality; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Dubnow's liberal-democratic civil-rights stance that shutdowns would be opposed.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Anachronistic and never addressed; the movement's non-socialist liberal wing might like it while the Bund's socialist wing would not.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Folkspartei programme demanded full civil and political equality, and Dubnow's liberal-democratic demands for the vote, in the Russian Empire's time, are read as including women.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Dubnow criticised religion as a base of Jewish nationhood but never claimed it oppressed women, so no position is inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; Dubnow's account of Jews as a nation defined by culture and history, not biology, leads to this inference.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources, so no position is inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The sources are silent on property theory and the Dubnowist strand was liberal-democratic without a documented view.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Anachronistic for the period; inferred from the demand for guaranteed rights for Jews and a liberal-democratic legal order.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from Dubnow's secular view of the Jews as a historical and cultural nation rather than a religious community.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the Folkspartei's liberal-democratic programme of equal rights, as no autonomy statement on gender is documented.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from Dubnow's non-socialist liberal programme; only the Bund took autonomism in a socialist direction and it is not the basis.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the Folkspartei's demand for democratic communal self-government and a national assembly.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the demand for equal civil rights and a national rather than religious definition of Jewry, which is at odds with a privileged church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Autonomism sought non-territorial national-cultural autonomy, so territorial autonomy was not its mechanism, though it did not oppose it.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The sources do not address plebiscites over disputed territory, and the doctrine was explicitly not territorial.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Anachronistic and outside the doctrine, which concerned minorities in multinational states.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from a modern liberal-national programme with no documented asceticism or self-sufficiency theme.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the demand for full civil and political rights for all, which cuts against restricting settlement by others.

equal-conscription.rationale: No conscription position is documented for the Dubnowist strand.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Dubnow's diaspora nationalism rooted the nation in culture and history rather than territory, though he valued a spiritual centre in Palestine.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Autonomism demanded full civil and legal rights within liberal-democratic states, which excludes killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Diaspora autonomism had no state foreign policy; this is anachronistic and gets no answer from the principles.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from Dubnow's emphasis on solidarity and defence of Jewish communities in every country, though the statement is framed for states.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Dubnow's version was liberal and non-socialist, but no resource doctrine appears in the sources.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the demand for individual civil and political rights alongside national rights.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: No tax policy is documented in the sources.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: No social-spending programme is documented, and the Bund and Folkspartei differed.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Autonomism rested on elected communal bodies and a party, the Folkspartei, so bypassing organised groups contradicts it.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the Folkspartei's liberal-democratic equality principles.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Dubnow grounded the nation in secular culture and history rather than religion, from which this is inferred.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Dubnow combined historical tradition and modern life, but the question is not addressed directly.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the Folkspartei's liberal reform outlook; divorce is not discussed in the sources.

national-resource-control.rationale: Resources are about territorial states, and autonomism sought non-territorial self-government.

missingStatements.text: A nation can survive as a people through its culture, history and institutions without possessing a territory or state of its own.
missingStatements.rationale: Dubnow's theory of a spiritual nation that has passed beyond the tribal and territorial-political stages is the doctrine's core, and no statement states it directly.

missingStatements.text: Members of a national minority should be guaranteed collective rights, such as a legal national assembly, in addition to equal individual rights.
missingStatements.rationale: Autonomists held that Jews should hold rights both as individuals and as members of their national groups, and the Folkspartei sought a Russia-wide Jewish national assembly.

missingStatements.text: A people's culture is best preserved if it develops in a language its people actually speak, rather than in a revived ancient one.
missingStatements.rationale: Autonomists stressed Yiddish, the living language of Eastern European Jewry, as the instrument of national culture.

notes: Dubnow's agnostic, secular-historical outlook was not shared by all autonomists; the Bund version was socialist and secularist, while religious Jews also supported communal autonomy. Late Dubnow grew more receptive to a Palestinian cultural centre, and the Hebrew 1937 edition of the Letters softened his anti-Zionism.
